comments.author: @woodedlane
comments.text: The cable cars were put in because the rich wanted the best view on top of Nob Hill and horse and carriage could not get up there.  If you ever visit Sf, the cable car museum is a must see.  The sea lions moved in after the 89 Loma prieta quake.  Initially they tried to get them to leave but finally gave in and they've been at Pier 39 ever since.  It's like they wanted to be the next tourist attraction.  And if you visit and take the cable car, the best one is the Powell/Hyde because it takes you up above crooked Lombard where there are great views.  The Powell/Mason ends up at the same place, but from a lower route.  SF has this thing about roof space for high rises for the public.  Check out public roof tops - and Salesforce Tower has a whole upscale garden path that goes for blocks.  Just so much to see and experience here.  I love my city of the last 40 years.  Just a nice bunch of people from every corner of the Earth hanging out together laughing eating and sharing stories.  I started out on a farm in the midwest and am very happy I ended up here.  And finally, not 10 blocks from where I live is a French bakery that Bon appetit named as best in the U.S. and I would have to agree. :)
